findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button> appears at line 81, before the submit button at line 92
findings.fix: Remove the View details button from the form, or move it after the submit button and style it to be clearly less prominent than the primary submit action.
findings.violation: The View details button, a secondary action, is placed in the middle of the form before the fields end, and carries explicit padding and font-size styling while the primary submit button has no styling. This interferes with action hierarchy by placing a secondary action prominently within the form rather than after all fields.

findings.fix: Collect the house number and street together in one address-line field.
findings.violation: The house number has its own field separate from the street, and it is required, so an address with no number cannot be entered.

findings.fix: Replace it with the standard token for this field, for example email.
findings.violation: The autocomplete value e-mail is not a valid autofill detail in the HTML standard, so autofill is broken for this field.

findings.evidence: The form asks for 'Full name' at line 11-12 and 'Your name' at line 70-71, both inferred as name fields. The form also includes 'How did you hear about us?' at line 83-90, 'Company website' at line 44-45, 'Organization name' at line 74-75, and 'Preferred contact time' at line 78-79.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate 'Your name' field (keep 'Full name'). Remove 'How did you hear about us?' unless marketing feedback is part of account creation. Clarify or remove unnecessary fields like 'Company website', 'Organization name', and 'Preferred contact time' unless they are essential to the account creation task.
findings.violation: The form asks for a name twice, under 'Full name' and 'Your name', doubling the work for this answer. It also asks for 'How did you hear about us?', marketing information the account creation task does not use.

findings.fix: Label the button with the action it performs, such as Create account or Send message.
findings.violation: The form's primary button is labelled Submit, a generic word that says nothing about what pressing it does.
On this name field, autocorrection and spellchecking stay on, so a phone keyboard can change a value it does not know.

findings.fix: Remove the confirmation field and offer a control that shows the password as typed.
findings.violation: The form asks for the new password a second time to confirm it, doubling the typing for every person.

findings.evidence: <label id="contacttime-label" for="contacttime-input" style="display:block">Preferred contact time</label> has display:block styling, while other labels like <label id="name-label" for="name-input">Full name</label> have no positioning declarations.
findings.fix: Apply consistent label positioning throughout the form. Choose either all labels above fields or all labels beside fields, and apply the same CSS rule to all labels.
findings.violation: The form mixes label alignments. The 'Preferred contact time' label declares display:block (above), while other labels have no CSS positioning and default to inline (beside their fields).

findings.fix: Increase the button's padding or overall dimensions to meet the recommended 44-48 CSS pixel size for touch targets. For example, use padding:16px 24px or increase the font-size.
findings.violation: The View details button with padding of 12px and font-size of 16px renders at approximately 40 CSS pixels in height, below the recommended 44-48 pixels for a comfortable touch target on mobile devices.
